blocking.issue: This is a regression from the L1-1 fix. The implicit ACK and the reconnect branch compare only the digest, not (`storeEpoch`, `assignmentSeq`). The owning document relies on assignments that keep the digest and change only signatures and sequences. Key rotation re-signs assignments 'at the next sequences, sent as a `Delta` with empty `ops`', and emergency removal opens a higher `storeEpoch` and re-signs 'at once, awaiting no ACK'. Suppose that empty-ops Delta is lost or the stream breaks. (1) The next Heartbeat reports the unchanged digest and is counted as the Ack, so the ACK timeout never re-sends it. (2) On reconnect, Figure 2's `same` test is true (active digest equals the assigned digest), so the replica records an implicit Ack and sends nothing. The Node therefore never gets the re-signed assignment. Under rotation, it keeps reporting the old `signingKeyId`, so step 3 (old key retires) stalls. Under emergency removal, it keeps an assignment accepted from the compromised key after `compromisedSince`. After its next restart it refuses to boot that Last-Known-Good and stays not ready until the Control Stream delivers. That is the P9 outage the re-sign was meant to prevent. The ACK row even says the record is keyed 'per (`node.id`, `storeEpoch`, `assignmentSeq`)', but the match it describes ignores both keys. And the owning document's `Heartbeat` does not carry them.
blocking.evidence: ACK/NACK row: "`Ack` means active, not durable, and counts per (`node.id`, `storeEpoch`, `assignmentSeq`), not per stream: a `Hello` or `Heartbeat` reporting the pending assignment's digest is its `Ack`, so a lost `Ack` never makes a Node lag." Figure 2: `same{"Active digest equals the assigned digest?"}` -- yes --> `none["Record the implicit Ack, send nothing; HeartbeatReply carries the promotion"]`. Figure 1: `alt active digest already assigned` / `R->>R: record the implicit Ack for this assignment` / `R-->>N: nothing to send`. Owning document, Revision signing, Rotation: "re-signs retained Revisions, assignments and promotions at the next sequences, sent as a `Delta` with empty `ops`. (3) The old key retires once those Nodes report the new `signingKeyId`"; Emergency removal: "opening a higher `storeEpoch` ... re-signs at once, awaiting no ACK. A Node refuses to boot a candidate or Last-Known-Good whose assignment or promotion it accepted from that key after `compromisedSince`". Owning document, message table: `Heartbeat` fields are "`activeDigest`, `lkgDigest`, `signingKeyId` per digest, `schemaLevels`, `ready`, `draining`, counters per `rolloutId`" (no `storeEpoch` or `assignmentSeq`).
blocking.fix: In the ACK/NACK row, replace "a `Hello` or `Heartbeat` reporting the pending assignment's digest is its `Ack`" with "a `Hello` matching the pending assignment's digest, `storeEpoch` and `assignmentSeq` is its `Ack`, and a Node re-ACKs a re-sent assignment it already runs". Retries then recover a lost Ack while the stream stays up, and Heartbeat no longer counts. If Heartbeat-based ACKs are wanted, add to More information's Proposed amendments that the owning document's `Heartbeat` gains `storeEpoch` and `assignmentSeq`, and match on all three. In Figure 2, relabel `same` as "Active digest, storeEpoch and assignmentSeq equal the committed assignment?"; a Node that is only behind on sequence then falls through to the Delta branch (empty `ops`). In Figure 1, relabel the first alt as "active digest and sequences already current". In Confirmation's integration tests, add "a Node that missed an empty-ops re-sign `Delta` receives it after reconnecting". The body is about 1,499 words under the verifier's rule, against a maximum of 1,500, and Mermaid labels do not count. Keep the prose change close to word-neutral, and do not remove text that resolved L1-1 to L1-3.

non_blocking.suggestion: "forbidigo bans grpc-go server APIs in `ruralz-control`" is stated as a current fact, but the Repository layout linter table limits forbidigo to `fmt.Print*` and the deprecated `x/net/http2` `Server` and `Transport`. The tech stack's Figure 2 shows `ruralz-control` does not link grpc-go at all, so a depguard rule banning `google.golang.org/grpc` under `cmd/ruralz-control` and `internal/control/...` is simpler. Add either rule to the Proposed amendments for Repository layout and conventions, next to the go-control-plane ban.

Ruralz Control cannot tell from a `Hello` that 'Last-Known-Good or active content fails re-hash', because the owning document's `Hello` has no such field. Its Drift table instead reports a local re-hash failure as `Nack` RZ-CFG-027. Say that the Node reports it that way, for example "after a `Nack` RZ-CFG-027 for a `Delta` or a local re-hash", so the decision in Figure 2 reads a signal the protocol actually carries.

"this Stream supersedes older ones for its node.id" can hold only within one replica. A half-open stream on another replica is not seen until HTTP/2 pings or the leader's status view catch it. Scope the rule to the replica, or add that the leader keys ACK and status by `node.id` so a duplicate stream on another replica changes nothing.

"a newer assignment replaces an unsent one" does not cover a Snapshot that is partly sent. State whether the replica finishes it and then supersedes it, or aborts it and starts the newer one under a new nonce.

`ReadTimeout` and `WriteTimeout` are server-wide on `http.Server`, so disabling them on 8091 also removes them from the unauthenticated unary `Enroll`. Keep `ReadHeaderTimeout` and `IdleTimeout`, and bound `Enroll` with a per-request deadline through `http.ResponseController`.
